newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to pay Ukraine $100 mln/year for navy base.
newsitem.headline: Russia to pay Ukraine $100 mln/year for navy base.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Foreign Minister Boris Pastukhov said on Thursday Russia would pay rent totalling $98-100 million annually to Ukraine for the lease of its Black Sea naval base at Sevastopol.
"The sum works out at about $98-100 million a year," Pastukhov told a round table discussion in Moscow.

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin signed a deal with his Ukrainian counterpart Pavlo Lazarenko on Wednesday in which Ukraine will lease the base on the Crimean peninsula to Russia for 20 years.
At the time of the signing, both premiers declined to outline the financial details of the deal.

While the lease of the base and shareout of the Black Sea Fleet agreed on Wednesday appears to have paved the way for the signing of a long-delayed friendship treaty between the two Slav states this weekend, many earlier deals over the disputed port have crumbled.
The port and fleet have been a major bone of contention between Moscow and Kiev ever since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Pastukhov added that part of the rent would be taken out of Ukraine's debts for oil and gas to Russia, which he said amounted to $526 million.
